questions.q: What does an adjustment do in Oracle Fusion Receivables?
options: Creates a brand-new invoice for the customer
Changes the balance due on a specific transaction directly, without a receipt or credit memo
Automatically reverses a receipt
Merges two customer accounts together
questions.explain: An adjustment is a direct correction tool that changes a transaction's balance due without involving a receipt or a separate credit transaction.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of a negative adjustment?
options: Correcting an invoice that was keyed for too low an amount
Waiving a small freight charge dispute
Adding a late fee outside the normal invoicing flow
Creating a new debit memo for an NSF check
questions.explain: A negative adjustment reduces the balance due, such as waiving a small disputed charge — the more common type of adjustment.

questions.q: What type of Receivables Activity must be assigned to an adjustment?
options: Miscellaneous Cash
Late Charge
Adjustment
Receipt Write-off
questions.explain: An adjustment requires a Receivables Activity of type Adjustment, which determines the GL account that absorbs the balance change.

questions.q: What is the purpose of approval limits on adjustments?
options: To prevent any adjustments from ever being created
To cap how large an adjustment a given user can create or approve without escalation
To determine which currency a transaction uses
To set the due date on a new invoice
questions.explain: Approval limits, defined per user (often by currency), cap how large an adjustment a person can post without routing it to a supervisor for approval.

questions.q: Why might a company use an adjustment instead of a credit memo for a small freight dispute?
options: Because credit memos cannot reduce a balance due
Because an adjustment is a lighter-weight correction tool, avoiding the overhead of a full separate transaction
Because adjustments are always larger in dollar amount than credit memos
Because credit memos require a receipt to be entered first
questions.explain: An adjustment is meant for small, policy-governed corrections where creating an entirely new transaction (a credit memo) would be unnecessary overhead.
